papers.paper: Hanich et al., 2014 — Why We Like to Watch Sad Films. The Pleasure of Being Moved in Aesthetic Experiences. Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts.
papers.description: Experiencing intense negative emotions (sadness, fear, tension, disgust) through fiction is paradoxically pleasurable because the brain registers the safety of the fictional frame. The emotional arousal is real but the threat is not — this gap creates catharsis. Sad films can amplify grief then release it. Horror films discharge anger or stress safely. Do NOT confuse with masochism in the clinical sense — this is about aesthetic pleasure in difficult emotions.

papers.paper: Algoe & Haidt, 2009 — Witnessing Excellence in Action: The 'Other-Praising' Emotions of Elevation, Gratitude, and Admiration. Journal of Positive Psychology.
papers.description: Witnessing extraordinary moral beauty, virtue, or human excellence — even in fiction — triggers a warm, uplifting sensation in the chest and a strong motivation to be a better person. It is distinct from happiness (which is about personal gain) — elevation is specifically triggered by other people's goodness. Reduces cynicism and discouragement powerfully. Best triggered by stories of radical kindness, sacrifice, or quiet heroism.

papers.paper: Stellar et al., 2015 — Self-Transcendent Emotions and Their Social Functions: Compassion, Gratitude, and Awe Bind Us to Others and to Our Humanity. Emotion.
papers.description: Exposure to something vast, complex, or beautiful that challenges one's current mental frameworks produces awe. Awe shrinks the perceived size of the self and its problems, reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines (physical stress markers), expands perceived time, and increases curiosity. Best triggered by cosmic scale (space docs), natural vastness, extraordinary complexity, or sublime beauty. Very effective for anxiety and overwhelm because it makes personal worries feel small.

papers.paper: Green & Brock, 2000 — The Role of Transportation in the Persuasiveness of Public Narratives. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
papers.description: Complete absorption in a narrative world reduces self-consciousness, mental chatter, and rumination. The more fully a person is transported, the stronger the emotional and attitudinal change — even toward challenging or dark stories. Transport is maximized by: vivid imagery, coherent plot, relatable protagonist, and immersive atmosphere. Best for overthinking, confusion, and restlessness — the mind needs something compelling enough to stop spinning.

papers.paper: Giles, 2002 — Parasocial Interaction: A Review of the Literature and a Model for Future Research. Media Psychology.
papers.description: One-sided emotional bonds with fictional characters activate the same neural systems as real friendships: they satisfy belonging needs, create a felt sense of being known, and reduce loneliness. The bond strengthens with repeated exposure (hence re-watching). Most powerful for loneliness and social isolation. Distinct from social_surrogate: parasocial focuses on the bond with specific characters; social_surrogate focuses on the familiar background presence of a known show.

papers.paper: Zillmann, 1988 — Mood Management Through Communication Choices. American Behavioral Scientist.
papers.description: Counter-intuitively, exposure to a mood slightly DIFFERENT from one's current emotional state is often more therapeutic than mood-matching. Someone deeply anxious benefits more from something melancholic-but-beautiful than from more anxiety or from forced comedy. The slight shift creates distance from the stuck state. This is the mechanism behind recommending something unexpected — it should feel like a gentle pivot, not an escape. High surprise_factor recommendations often use this mechanism.

papers.paper: Aron et al., 1992 — Inclusion of Other in the Self Scale and the Structure of Interpersonal Closeness. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
papers.description: Engaging with perspectives, identities, or worlds radically different from one's own expands the psychological self and generates a felt sense of growth and possibility. Most powerful for boredom, emptiness, feeling stuck, or loss of meaning. Works best with stories set in very different cultures, historical periods, or social contexts — the greater the distance from the user's daily reality, the stronger the expansion effect. Doubt and confusion also respond well to self-expansion.

papers.paper: Chu & Downes, 2000 — Odour-Evoked Autobiographical Memories: Psychological Investigations of Proustian Phenomena. Chemical Senses.
papers.description: Specific sensory details — a melody, a visual palette, a texture, an ambient sound — can bypass conscious recall and trigger vivid, emotionally rich autobiographical memories. This is the Proustian mechanism: a madeleine dipped in tea unlocks an entire world. In film/music/books, works with a strong, distinctive sensory signature matched to the user's formative years (nostalgia window: ages 8–16) are most powerful. Most effective for nostalgia, melancholy, and grief — it creates felt continuity with the past self.

papers.paper: Sedikides & Wildschut, 2018 — Finding Meaning in Nostalgia. Review of General Psychology.
papers.description: Nostalgia is a bittersweet, self-relevant, social emotion triggered by remembering meaningful past experiences. It increases perceived self-continuity (the sense that past and present self are the same person), social connectedness, and sense of meaning. It counteracts loneliness, emptiness, and meaninglessness. Most effective for content from the user's own nostalgia window (birth year + 8 to + 16). Distinct from involuntary_memory: nostalgia is the deliberate emotional tone of the work; involuntary_memory is the sensory trigger mechanism.

papers.paper: Derrick, Gabriel & Hugenberg, 2009 — Social Surrogacy: How Favored Television Programs Provide the Experience of Belonging. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology.
papers.description: Familiar TV shows and beloved books can function as social surrogates: their recurring characters and settings provide a felt sense of belonging, comfort, and not being alone. Revisiting a known show is more effective than watching something new — the familiarity itself is the therapeutic agent. In controlled studies, this reduced loneliness by ~23%. Best for exhaustion, loneliness, and emotional overwhelm — when someone needs comfort more than stimulation. Distinct from parasocial: social_surrogate is about the comforting ambient presence of a familiar world, not a bond with specific characters.

papers.paper: Raposa et al., 2016 — Prosocial Behavior Mitigates the Negative Effects of Stress in Everyday Life. Clinical Psychological Science.
papers.description: Stories centered on acts of kindness, cooperation, solidarity, or altruism activate reward circuits and reduce ruminative thinking. The viewer/reader vicariously participates in prosocial acts, which generates a mild but real boost in well-being. Most effective for cynicism, discouragement, guilt, and self-disgust — states where the person has lost faith in human goodness (including their own). Distinct from elevation: prosocial focuses on ordinary everyday kindness; elevation focuses on extraordinary moral beauty.

novels.author: Helen Fielding

Through her intimate diary, you aren't just reading a story—you're gaining a confidante who truly understands the chaos of being single. Meet the friend who knows exactly how you feel.

novels.title: The Rosie Project
novels.paper: Giles, 2002 — Parasocial Interaction: A Review of the Literature and a Model for Future Research. Media Psychology.
novels.why: Bonding with Don Tillman's unique perspective helps you feel less alone through a charming parasocial connection.

And so, in the orderly, evidence-based manner with which Don approaches all things, he designs the Wife Project to find his perfect partner: a sixteen-page, scientifically valid survey to filter out the drinkers, the smokers, the late arrivers. Rosie Jarman is all these things. She also is strangely beguiling, fiery, and intelligent. And while Don quickly disqualifies her as a candidate for the Wife Project, as a DNA expert Don is particularly
novels.author: Graeme Simsion

When he meets the chaotic, spirited Rosie Jarman, his rigid walls begin to crumble. In a world that often overlooks them, Don and Rosie find the one thing science can't explain: the profound comfort of finally being seen.

novels.title: Eleanor Oliphant is Completely Fine
novels.paper: Raposa et al., 2016 — Prosocial Behavior Mitigates the Negative Effects of Stress in Everyday Life. Clinical Psychological Science.

Nothing is missing in her carefully timetabled life of avoiding social interactions, where weekends are punctuated by frozen pizza, vodka, and phone chats with Mummy. But everything changes when Eleanor meets Raymond, the bumbling and deeply unhygienic IT guy from her office. When she and Raymond together save Sammy, an elderly gentleman who has fallen on the sidewalk, the three become the kinds of friends who rescue
novels.author: Gail Honeyman
novels.overview_rewritten: Eleanor lives a rigid, lonely life until a chance act of kindness changes everything. After teaming up with her clumsy colleague Raymond to help a fallen stranger, Eleanor discovers the quiet joy of mutual support. Through small, everyday gestures of friendship and solidarity, she learns that no one has to face the world alone.

novels.title: Where the Crawdads Sing

Sensitive and intelligent, she has survived for years alone in the marsh that she calls home, finding friends in the gulls and lessons in the sand. Then the time comes when she yearns to be touched and loved. When two young men from town become intrigued by her wild beauty, Kya opens herself to a new life–until the unthinkable happen
novels.author: Delia Owens
novels.overview_rewritten: Abandoned in the salt-sprayed wilds of North Carolina, Kya Clark survives alone, reading the secrets of the marsh to soothe her solitude. But when a local golden boy is found dead, the town’s prejudice clashes with Kya’s fragile hope for love. In a world of shimmering tides and dark secrets, one girl must fight to prove she isn't the monster they imagined.

novels.title: Attachments
novels.paper: Giles, 2002 — Parasocial Interaction: A Review of the Literature and a Model for Future Research. Media Psychology.

They go on sending each other endless and endlessly hilarious e-mails, discussing every aspect of their personal lives. Meanwhile, Lincoln O'Neill can't believe this is his job now- reading other people's e-mail. When he applied to be "internet security officer," he pictured himself building firewalls and crushing hacke
novels.author: Rainbow Rowell
novels.overview_rewritten: Lincoln is the secret witness to every raw, hilarious, and intimate detail of Beth and Jennifer’s lives. As he reads their unfiltered thoughts, he becomes the only person who truly knows them—and they become the only world he wants to live in. In a city of millions, they are the only ones who make him feel less alone.

novels.title: Dandelion Wine
novels.paper: Chu & Downes, 2000 — Odour-Evoked Autobiographical Memories: Psychological Investigations of Proustian Phenomena. Chemical Senses.

novels.author: Ray Bradbury
novels.overview_rewritten: The scent of freshly mowed grass and the sharp tang of green apples collide in the summer of '28. For twelve-year-old Douglas Spaulding, life is a blur of gold-fuzzed bees, the sting of half-burnt firecrackers, and the warmth of Grandma’s kitchen. It is a sensory map of a childhood rediscovered—a timeless vintage of sorrows and marvels.

By turns overwhelming, sublime, heartbreaking, and uplifting, the daily experiences of the unforgettable Nolans are raw with honesty and
novels.author: Betty Smith
novels.overview_rewritten: In the crushing poverty of turn-of-the-century Williamsburg, young Francie Nolan discovers that the human spirit can bloom in the harshest soil. Through radical resilience and the quiet, selfless sacrifices of a family refusing to be broken by hardship, this is a testament to the enduring power of dignity and the transformative beauty of unconditional love.

novels.title: The Remains of the Day
novels.paper: Hanich et al., 2014 — Why We Like to Watch Sad Films. The Pleasure of Being Moved in Aesthetic Experiences. Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts.
novels.why: Allow these gentle regrets to guide you toward a healing catharsis through benign masochism.
novels.sensory_signature: The polished, hushed stillness of a great English estate
novels.overview: In the summer of 1956, Stevens, the ageing butler of Darlington Hall, embarks on a leisurely holiday that will take him deep into the countryside and into his past . . .A contemporary classic, The Remains of the Day is Kazuo Ishiguro's beautiful and haunting evocation of life between the wars in a Great English House, of lost causes and lost love.
novels.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
novels.overview_rewritten: An aging butler journeys through the English countryside, finally confronting the crushing weight of a lifetime spent in servitude. It is a devastating excavation of suppressed longing and the agonizing realization that the love he sacrificed for duty was the only thing that ever mattered.

To save
novels.author: Karen Russell
novels.overview_rewritten: Twelve-year-old Ava is drowning in the humid chaos of Swamplandia!, her family’s decaying alligator park in the Florida Everglades. Amidst the scent of sulfur and swamp water, she must wrangle seventy predators and a fractured family—including a sister haunted by a ghost and a brother betrayed by a rival empire—to survive the crushing weight of her mother's death.

novels.title: Educated
novels.paper: Algoe & Haidt, 2009 — Witnessing Excellence in Action: The 'Other-Praising' Emotions of Elevation, Gratitude, and Admiration. Journal of Positive Psychology.

novels.sensory_signature: The rugged, isolated atmosphere of the Idaho mountains
novels.overview: *Educated* is a 2018 memoir by the American author Tara Westover. Westover recounts overcoming her survivalist Mormon family in order to go to college, and emphasizes the importance of education in enlarging her world. She details her journey from her isolated life in the mountains of Idaho to completing a PhD program in history at Cambridge University. She started college at the age of 17 having had no formal education. She explores her struggle to reconcile her desire to learn with the world she inhabited with her father.
novels.author: Tara Westover
novels.overview_rewritten: Born into a world of isolation and survivalist hardship, Tara Westover courageously broke the bonds of her restrictive upbringing to pursue the light of knowledge. Her journey from an uneducated teenager to a Cambridge PhD is a testament to the indomitable human spirit and the quiet heroism required to redefine one's destiny through the transformative power of learning.

At twenty-two, Cheryl Strayed thought she'd lost everything when her mother died young of cancer. Her family scattered in their grief, her marriage was soon destroyed, and slowly her life spun out of control. Four years after her mother's death, with nothing more to lose, Strayed made the most impulsive decision of her life: to hike the Pacific Crest Trail from the Mojave Desert through California and Oregon to Washington State—a
novels.author: Cheryl Strayed

novels.overview_rewritten: Shattered by loss and adrift in a life unspooling, a young woman ventures alone into the crushing vastness of the Pacific Crest Trail. Across eleven hundred miles of primordial wilderness, the sublime scale of the American West dwarfs her grief, dissolving her broken identity into the infinite beauty of the wild to forge a soul reborn.

novels.title: Siddhartha

novels.overview: Hermann Hesse wrote Siddhartha after he traveled to India in the 1910s. It tells the story of a young boy who travels the country in a quest for spiritual enlightenment in the time of Guatama Buddha. It is a compact, lyrical work, which reads like an allegory about the finding of wisdom.
novels.author: Hermann Hesse
novels.overview_rewritten: Journey into the timeless expanse of ancient India, where a young seeker traverses the boundary between the finite self and the infinite cosmos. In the shadow of the Buddha, Siddhartha pursues a wisdom that transcends human language, dissolving individual ego into the sublime, rhythmic flow of the universe.

It is seen as the archetypal modern African novel in English, and one of the first to receive global critical acclaim. It is a staple book in schools throughout Africa and is widely read and studied in English-speaking countries around the world. The novel was first published in the UK in 1962 by William Heinemann Ltd, and became the first work published in Heinemann's African
novels.author: Chinua Achebe
novels.overview_rewritten: Step into the ancestral heart of pre-colonial Nigeria, a world governed by rigid honor, spiritual depths, and complex tribal laws. Experience the visceral collision between an ancient civilization and the arrival of European settlers, challenging everything you know about identity, power, and the fragility of a world unraveling.

novels.title: The God of Small Things

The book explores how the small things affect people's behavior and their lives. The book also reflects its irony against casteism, which is a major discrimination that prevails in India. It won the Booker Prize in 1997.
novels.author: Arundhati Roy
novels.overview_rewritten: Two innocent twins are crushed by the ruthless "Love Laws" of a society that dictates who is allowed to be loved and how much. In a world of suffocating caste prejudice, the smallest cruelties unravel their lives, offering a devastating exploration of grief, longing, and the exquisite ache of a childhood shattered by forbidden desire.

novels.title: Snow Country

novels.author: Yasunari Kawabata
novels.overview_rewritten: Amidst the crushing silence of a frozen wilderness, a fleeting human passion collides with the timeless, sublime beauty of the Japanese Alps. This Nobel Prize-winning masterpiece dissolves the boundaries of the self, immersing the reader in a world of ethereal landscapes and crystalline longing. It is a haunting meditation on the fragility of life against the vast, indifferent majesty of nature.

novels.title: The Alchemist
novels.paper: Aron et al., 1992 — Inclusion of Other in the Self Scale and the Structure of Interpersonal Closeness. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.

novels.author: Douglas Adams

Guided by an infinite electronic encyclopedia, he traverses the staggering complexity of a universe where human existence is a mere footnote, discovering that the secrets of life are as vast and absurd as the stars themselves.

Experience a sublime, zany descent into the infinite, where the scale of the galaxy renders our smallest worries invisible.

novels.author: Terry Pratchett

It is a cozy, bureaucratic tragedy about the end of everything.

novels.title: Catch-22

novels.author: Joseph Heller

This harrowing descent into the absurdity of war oscillates between manic laughter and visceral horror, offering a devastatingly sane perspective on the agony of existence. Experience the crushing weight of a system where the only escape is madness.

novels.title: Hyperbole and a Half

novels.author: Allie Brosh
novels.overview_rewritten: Finally, someone who sees the world exactly as you do. Step inside the beautifully absurd mind of Allie Brosh, where raw vulnerability and leaping wit turn the loneliness of complex emotions into a shared, intimate conversation. Through her iconic illustrations, you aren't just reading a book—you're finding the friend who truly understands you.

novels.title: The Bell Jar
novels.paper: Hanich et al., 2014 — Why We Like to Watch Sad Films. The Pleasure of Being Moved in Aesthetic Experiences. Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts.

novels.sensory_signature: suffocating, sultry heat

novels.author: Sylvia Plath
novels.overview_rewritten: A brilliant young woman descends into a suffocating, visceral spiral of madness, trapped beneath the distorting glass of her own mind. It is a devastatingly raw portrait of psychological collapse that invites you to dwell in the depths of despair, only to find a haunting, cathartic release in the wreckage.

As the police gather outside, the anxious strangers huddled within try to make the best of a ve
novels.author: Fredrik Backman
novels.overview_rewritten: On New Year's Eve, a clumsy bank robber takes a group of anxious strangers hostage in a luxury apartment. Amidst the tension, these lonely, fractured souls find an unexpected kinship, offering one another the kindness and understanding they've lacked. In a moment of shared vulnerability, they discover that no one is truly alone when they choose to look after each other.

novels.title: The Blue Castle
novels.paper: Aron et al., 1992 — Inclusion of Other in the Self Scale and the Structure of Interpersonal Closeness. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
novels.why: Valene's journey toward self-actualization offers a beautiful sense of growth and possibility through self-expansion.
novels.sensory_signature: The lush, wild landscapes of the Canadian wilderness
novels.overview: Valancy Stirling is 29, unmarried, and has never been in love. Living with her overbearing mother and meddlesome aunt, she finds her only consolation in the "forbidden" books of John Foster and her daydreams of the Blue Castle--a place where all her dreams come true and she can be who she truly wants to be. After getting shocking news from the doctor, she rebels against her family and discovers a surprising new world, full of love and adventures far beyond her most secret dreams.
novels.author: Lucy Maud Montgomery
novels.overview_rewritten: Trapped in a stifling, archaic world of familial duty and repression, Valancy Stirling escapes through forbidden texts into a vivid internal sanctuary. When a shocking diagnosis shatters her constraints, she abandons her colorless existence to plunge into a radical new reality of passion and wilderness, discovering a vast, uncharted version of herself far beyond her wildest imaginings.

So Tom moves back his to London, his old home, to become a high school history teacher--the perfect job for someone who has witnessed the city's history first hand. novels.author: Matt Haig
novels.overview_rewritten: Tom Hazard has witnessed the crushing weight of centuries, from the ink of Shakespeare’s quill to the vast horizons of Captain Cook’s voyages. Now a history teacher in London, he navigates a world of fleeting moments while harboring a timeless secret. But as a forbidden romance ignites, a clandestine society emerges to hunt the man who has outlived the ages.

novels.title: The enchanted April
novels.paper: Raposa et al., 2016 — Prosocial Behavior Mitigates the Negative Effects of Stress in Everyday Life. Clinical Psychological Science.
novels.why: Let these blossoming female friendships remind you of human goodness through the warmth of prosocial connection.
novels.sensory_signature: Sun-drenched Italian landscapes
novels.overview: "A notice in The Times addressed to 'Those Who Appreciate Wistaria and Sunshine' advertises a 'small medieval Italian Castle to be let for the month of April'. Four very different women take up the offer: Mrs Wilkins and Mrs Arbuthnot, both fleeing unappreciative husbands; beautiful Lady Caroline, sick of being 'grabbed' by lovesick men; and the imperious, ageing Mrs Fisher. On the shores of the Mediterranean, beauty, warmth and leisure weave their spell, and nothing will ever be the same again." -- Provided by publisher.
novels.author: Elizabeth von Arnim
novels.overview_rewritten: Four lonely women, each burdened by the weight of unappreciated lives, gather at a medieval Italian castle for a month of shared sanctuary. In the warmth of the Mediterranean spring, they discover the quiet joy of supporting one another. Through simple acts of kindness and newfound solidarity, these strangers transform their isolation into a lasting, healing friendship.
